# Engine trouble codes (KA24DE and VG33E)

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Swap the ECM to match the supercharger setup for better fuel mapping. [t1326]

Swap a fuel injector from cylinder 4 into another location to address engine trouble codes. [t1316]

[Partial] Clear the code using a scanner, then observe if the SES light returns after staying off briefly. [t1289]

[Partial] Inspect the sensor located on top of the transmission to check if it is properly plugged back in. [t1289]

[Partial] Drive the vehicle for approximately 50 complete driving cycles to verify the light stays off. [t1298]

[Partial] Remove the intake manifold to replace any broken gaskets with red RTV sealant. [t1533]

Identify the SRS code pattern and interpret it as an airbag module malfunction. [t1594]

Connect a vehicle to a computer diagnostic machine and read any trouble codes displayed. [t1303]

[Partial] Disconnect the four oxygen sensors and drive about 4 miles until a new code appears. [t1303]

Pull the fuel pump fuse and start the engine a few times. [t2016]

Suck air from the radiator with a tester, wait two minutes for fluid reaction, then look for color change. [t2017]

[Partial] Check spark plugs, inspect plug wires, spray carburetor cleaner at intake gaskets, and examine distributor rotor connections. [t1503]

[Partial] Drive the vehicle approximately 50 miles on mixed terrain with a scan tool to activate engine readiness monitors. [t1503]

[Partial] Scan for O2 sensor circuit faults after installing new headers or cats. [t1089]

[Partial] Install upstream and downstream O2 sensors, extending wires or using eliminators as needed for custom setups. [t1687]

2. Start the engine a few times while the fuse is out.

2. [Partial] Wait two minutes for the fluid to react.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- If keeping a stock NA ECM, expect a rich idle and potential 'serial link fault' or turbo code if the BCS is missing. [t1326]
- [Partial] Run 92+ octane fuel to prevent knocking since the ECMS cannot limit boost in limp mode. [t1326]
- Clean the electronic portion of an injector in an ultrasonic parts washer before testing. [t1316]
- Note that some vehicles may require an OEM distributor to resolve the issue, as aftermarket or parts-store versions can be spotty. [t1303]
- [Partial] Use this method before removing components if you suspect high fuel pressure or flooding issues. [t2016]
- Look for color change in the coolant sample; blue indicates no combustion gas mixing. [t2017]
- [Partial] Use this negative result to rule out a blown head gasket before committing to expensive repairs. [t2017]
- [Partial] Spray carburetor cleaner around intake gaskets to check for leaks; the engine sound will change if a leak exists. [t1503]
- [Partial] Check distributor rotor connections and look for wobble. [t1503]
- Note: The system has no dash indicators for this specific check; the scan tool is required to confirm when monitors are ready. [t1503]
- [Partial] A total drive distance of around 50 miles seems sufficient, but a mix of highway and trail driving ensures coverage. [t1503]
- P161 indicates a problem with the heater control circuit. [t1089]
- P160 suggests no activity was detected by the sensor. [t1089]
- Extend the wire on one of the upstream sensors if necessary to reach the bung hole. [t1687]
- Use check engine light eliminators in mid-pipe setups to fool the computer into thinking primary cats are still working. [t1687]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Replacing all six injectors immediately after fixing just one faulty unit. [t1316]
- [Partial] Skipping the depressurization step, which can lead to messy fuel leaks during other repairs. [t2016]
- [Partial] Not waiting for the engine to warm up enough after replacing a regulator that dumps extra fuel into cylinder #6. [t2016]
- [Partial] Relying solely on oil dipstick readings which can yield false negatives or be inaccurate due to short length. [t2017]
